newsitem.title: JAPAN: IMF, Japan to give $10 bln for Thai aid--paper.
newsitem.headline: IMF, Japan to give $10 bln for Thai aid--paper.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Japan's Export-Import Bank and Japanese commercial banks will provide a total of $10 billion to support Thailand's ailing economy, a Japanese daily reported on Tuesday.

The Yomiuri Shimbun, quoting international financial sources, said the IMF and the ADB will together provide about $5 billion to the rescue package, while the Ex-Im Bank is expected to match whatever contribution the IMF makes.

The paper added that Japanese banks with branches in Thailand are expected to also coordinate to give several billion dollars in additional loans to help Bangkok shore up its foreign reserves and restructure its economy.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya has said Thailand is still talking to the IMF about the rescue package but the framework is expected to be worked ou and approved by the cabinet this week.
Thai officials have so far made no comment on whether they expect Japanese aid to be included in the package.
